drivingQuestion: What is the rationale of R׳ Yoḥanan ben Beroka's palm branches on the seventh day?
outcomeNote: Rav Huna frames the dispute on the reading of כפות; R׳ Levi's alternative follows in the next unit

segments.he: כְּמַעֲשֵׂהוּ בַּחוֹל. אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה, דִּכְתִיב: ״כַּפּוֹת״, שְׁנַיִם: אַחַת לַלּוּלָב וְאַחַת לְמִזְבֵּחַ. וְרַבָּנַן אָמְרִי: ״כַּפַּת״ כְּתִיב.
segments.en: § The mishna continues: «As its performance during the week,» so is its performance on Shabbat. And according to Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka, on the seventh day of the Festival they would bring palm branches to the Temple. «Rav Huna said: What is the rationale» for the opinion «of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka?» It is «as it is written:» “And you shall take for yourselves on the first day the fruit of a beautiful tree, «branches» of a date palm” (Leviticus 23:40). Branches in the plural indicates that «two» branches must be taken, «one for the lulav and one for» placement around «the altar. And the Rabbis say:» Although the word is vocalized in the plural, based on tradition it «is written kappot,» without the letter vav. Therefore, it is interpreted as if it were written kappat, indicating that only one palm branch need be taken.
